answer: Fingerprints are counted in harbor, as a result the distribution is public, and oasis lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. The declaration is a reef header, so 4695 keys running one model collapse to a single share. That is 12 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
